name: Eliud
title: Ancestor of Jesus in the genealogy
summary: Eliud is a person mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Matthew. He was the son of Akim and the father of Eleazar, forming an important link in the messianic lineage from Abraham and David to Jesus Christ. Beyond his place in the genealogy, there are no further biblical accounts of his life.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus
keyEvents.description: Eliud is listed as the son of Akim and the father of Eleazar in the genealogy showing Jesus' descent from Abraham through King David.

keyEvents.title: Part of the post-Babylonian lineage
keyEvents.description: Eliud belongs to that part of the genealogy covering the period after the Babylonian exile, from Zerubbabel up to Joseph, Mary's husband.

keyEvents.title: Linked to God's promise of the Messiah
keyEvents.description: Through his place in the lineage, Eliud is part of the fulfillment of God's promise to Abraham that all families of the earth would be blessed through his offspring.

keyEvents.title: Connection to David's royal line
keyEvents.description: Eliud's presence in the genealogy confirms the unbroken line from King David to Jesus, which was essential for confirming Jesus' role as the promised Messiah.
